United States men's FIBA World Championship team|National team]]}} }} '''Eric Ambrose Gordon Jr.''' (born December 25, 1988){{cite web|title=Eric Gordon Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gordoer01.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 8, 2020}} is a Bahamian-American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). In high school, he was named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] during his senior year while playing at [[North Central High School (Indianapolis)|North Central High School]]. He is known, in part, as the subject of a recruiting competition between the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois]] and [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana University]] in the spring and summer of 2006; because of Gordon's talent and high level of play that year, his recruitment was the subject of media coverage. Gordon played one season of [[college basketball]] at Indiana{{Cite web|url=http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20061108/SPORTS0601/61108017|title=Gordon seals IU deal with signing}} and was considered one of the top collegiate players in the nation that year.[https://web.archive.org/web/20070113004213/http://www.cstv.com/hoopsodyssey/2007/01/08/ Eric Gordon: Before the Storm] He finished his freshman season leading the [[Big Ten]] in scoring and tied for 19th in the nation at 21.5 points per game.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/stats/player?season=2008 |access-date=April 21, 2023 |title=NCAA College Basketball Statistics: 2007–2008 Men's Basketball Leaders – Points}} Gordon entered the [[2008 NBA draft]] and was selected seventh overall by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. ==Early life== Gordon was born in [[Indianapolis]]. At age four, he began playing sports at the [[Jewish Community Center]] across the street from his home, starting with soccer and then quickly moving on to basketball. At age seven he began playing competitive basketball at the Municipal Gardens. It was at the JCC that Gordon announced his departure from college to enter his name into the [[NBA draft]].{{cite web|last=Berkman|first=Jacob|title=From the JCC to the NBA|url=https://www.jta.org/2008/04/08/arts-entertainment/from-the-jcc-to-the-nba|website=Jewish Telegraphic Agency|date=April 8, 2008|access-date=March 6, 2016}} ===High school=== [[File:20070305 Eric Gordon.jpg|thumb|180px|right|Gordon in 2007 as a high school basketball player]] Gordon attended Fox Hill Elementary School, down the street from his childhood home. He then attended Northview Middle School and [[North Central High School (Indianapolis, Indiana)|North Central High School]], where he played varsity basketball all four years. North Central's 2007 game against [[Loyola Academy]] of [[Wilmette, Illinois]] which featured [[Michael Jordan]]'s sons, Jeffrey and Marcus, was aired on ESPN. He scored a record high of 43 points that night. He later went on to score 50 points twice during the season. He led North Central to the Indiana 4A title game his senior year. They fell to [[E'Twaun Moore]], Angel Garcia and East Chicago Central. Gordon averaged 29 points, 6.2 rebounds and 3.3 assists while shooting 57.0% from the field, 77.9% from the free-throw line, and 46.2% from three-point range. He was named Indiana's [[Indiana "Mr. Basketball" award|"Mr. Basketball"]] for 2007 as well as a McDonald's All-American. Rivals.com ranked him the nation's #2 high school prospect in the class of 2007, behind [[Michael Beasley]].{{cite web |url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1611 |title=Rivals.com Rivals150 2007 |publisher=Rivals.com |access-date=March 10, 2011 |archive-date=September 25, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080925232402/http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1611 |url-status=dead }} During the summer, Gordon attended many AAU tournaments, Adidas Superstar camps, and Big Time in Las Vegas. He played on teams that included future NBA players [[Mike Conley Jr.]], [[Josh McRoberts]], [[Daequan Cook]], [[Derrick Rose]] and [[Greg Oden]]. ===Recruitment=== In 2005 as a sophomore in high school, Gordon made an early verbal commitment to [[Bruce Weber (coach)|Bruce Weber]], who had somewhat recently replaced Bill Self as the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|University of Illinois]]' head coach when Self left to accept the head coaching position at Kansas. On November 30, 2005,{{cite news |title=Indianapolis standout commits to Illini early |url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=SL&p_theme=sl&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=10E3EE544D202350&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D |access-date=January 1, 2008 |work=St. Louis Post-Dispatch |date=December 1, 2005 |archive-date=July 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240704103633/https://www.newslibrary.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=SL&p_theme=sl&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=10E3EE544D202350&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date%3AD |url-status=dead }} Gordon made a verbal commitment to play basketball for Weber at Illinois, despite overtures from [[Duke University|Duke]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] and [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]].{{cite web|title=Illini are starting to reap recruiting rewards |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=39568 |access-date=January 1, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081227031130/http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=39568 |archive-date=December 27, 2008 }} Gordon and his family cited their comfort with Weber, the relatively short distance to the Illinois campus from their Indianapolis home, and the success of former Illini guards [[Deron Williams]] and [[Luther Head]] in the NBA as reasons for their decision.{{cite web |title=How Gordon came to IU |access-date=February 9, 2008 |url=http://blogs.indystar.com/recruiting/2006/10/how_gordon_came_to_iu.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061124101245/http://blogs.indystar.com/recruiting/2006/10/how_gordon_came_to_iu.html |archive-date=November 24, 2006}} On February 15, 2006, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' reported that [[Mike Davis (basketball, born 1960)|Mike Davis]], then the head coach at [[Indiana University (Bloomington)|Indiana University]], intended to resign after the 2005–06 season, due in part to a lack of support after the team failed to make the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] in 2004 and 2005.{{cite news |title=Seth Davis: Mike Davis out at Indiana |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/writers/seth_davis/02/15/indiana.davis/?cnn=yes |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604013724/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/writers/seth_davis/02/15/indiana.davis/?cnn=yes |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 4, 2011 |access-date=January 1, 2008 | work=CNN | date=February 15, 2006}} Indiana subsequently hired [[Kelvin Sampson]] as the new men's basketball coach in March 2006.{{cite web |title=Sampson brings in assistants with Indiana ties |date = April 13, 2006|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2407816 |access-date=January 1, 2008}} Some reporters speculated that Gordon was uninterested in playing at Indiana under Mike Davis because of Davis's lack of success. Shortly after Sampson was named head coach, he hired Jeff Meyer, Eric Gordon Sr.'s college basketball coach and a longtime family friend, as an assistant.{{cite news |title=Gordon's switch to Indiana highlights hectic week before Midnight Madness |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/recruiting/basketball/national/2006-10-17-basketball.htm |access-date=February 14, 2008 | work=USA Today | date=October 18, 2006 |first=Jerry |last=Meyer}} During the subsequent offseason, Gordon was recruited by Sampson's staff after Gordon told Sampson he was again interested in Indiana. It was rumored in July 2006 that Gordon was considering opting out of his verbal commitment to Illinois because of concerns about the quality of Weber's Illinois recruiting class,{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=107419 |title=Sifting through summer camp gossip |access-date=January 1, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081227031224/http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=107419 |archive-date=December 27, 2008 }} but Gordon said that although he was a childhood fan of the Hoosiers and was considering Indiana, he was still committed to Illinois.{{cite web |url=http://media.www.dailyillini.com/media/storage/paper736/news/2006/09/28/Sports/Column.Eric.Gordon.Will.He.Wear.Orange.And.Blue.In.2007-2313436.shtml |title=Eric Gordon: Will He Wear Orange and Blue in 2007? |access-date=December 31, 2007}}{{dead link|date=October 2010}} During that same month, Gordon played with fellow top-5 recruit [[Derrick Rose]] in an attempt to convince Rose to join him at Illinois, but Rose declined the offer.{{cite web |url=http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2006/jul/07/keegan_chicagoan_targeted_self/?sports |title=Keegan: Chicagoan targeted by Self |access-date=January 1, 2008}} Rumors of an impending IU commitment continued into the start of the 2006–07 academic year, fueled in part by Gordon's rise to the top of some services' rankings of high school basketball players and the reemergent Indiana Hoosier basketball program.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/blog/Samueltstory/tag/EricGordonRecruitingSaga |title=The Eric Gordon Saga |access-date=January 1, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081227031314/http://www.sportingnews.com/blog/Samueltstory/tag/EricGordonRecruitingSaga |archive-date=December 27, 2008 }} On September 2, 2006, Gordon and Rose made an unofficial visit to Indiana to scrimmage with Hoosier players,{{cite web |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-150868779.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102233756/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-150868779.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=November 2, 2012 |title=IU hosts potential basketball recruits: Two highly ranked prep players scrimmaged with the team Saturday |via=[[HighBeam Research]] |url-access=subscription |work=The News-Sentinel |date=September 4, 2006 |location=Fort Wayne, IN |access-date=January 1, 2008}} fueling further speculation that Gordon would switch his commitment. Six weeks later, on October 13, 2006, Eric Sr. announced that his son had officially decided to do so.{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/bigten/2006-10-13-indiana-gordon_x.htm?POE=SPOISVA |title=Prep star Eric Gordon changes mind, makes move to Hoosiers |access-date=January 1, 2008 | work=USA Today | date=October 13, 2006 |first=Jeff |last=Rabjohns}} Gordon signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] with Indiana on November 8, 2006.{{cite news |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/sioncampus/11/08/college/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080204011917/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/sioncampus/11/08/college/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 4, 2008 |title=Truth & Rumors: Murdered Miami DL Pata owned gun collection |access-date=January 1, 2008 | work=CNN | date=November 8, 2006}} ===Aftermath=== Gordon's announcement gave Indiana a very strong 2007 recruiting class, ranked by some analysts as the third-best incoming class in the country.{{cite news |url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=CSTB&p_theme=cstb&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=1154C43BDA6DD6B0&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM |title=Gordon could be swing man: Switch from Illini to Hoosiers a huge impact}}{{dead link|date=July 2025}} Sampson and Weber both received criticism from fellow coaches for failing to communicate with one another about Gordon's recruitment.{{cite web |url=http://www.madison.com/archives/read.php?ref=/tct/2006/10/30/0610300151.php |title=Hoosiers-Illini Recruiting Feud a Hot Topic |access-date=January 1, 2008}} Although the NCAA does not regulate verbal commitments or the recruitment of orally committed players, some observers have claimed that Sampson acted unethically in recruiting a committed player without first contacting Weber.{{cite web |url=http://www.sportsline.com/columns/story/10411974 |access-date=February 9, 2008 |title=A few wins gets Sampson some cheating immunity |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071018071627/http://www.sportsline.com/columns/story/10411974 |archive-date=October 18, 2007 }} The timing of the switch was particularly damaging for Illinois, which had planned for Gordon to be part of its class, and was left without a shooting guard at a time when other guards had made verbal commitments.{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/2006-11-08-signing-day-roundup_x.htm |title=Signing day roundup: Florida, Louisville, Michigan State bring in talent |access-date=January 1, 2008 | work=USA Today | date=November 8, 2006}} The Illini received a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] from top 100 shooting guard Quinton Watkins of Compton, California, the following December,{{cite news |url=http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-30334793_ITM |title=Eureka! Watkins goes east: Illini recruit will be only 3rd player from Calif. in school history |access-date=January 1, 2008}} but, due to [[NCAA]] Academic Clearinghouse issues, he did not play for the Illini, eventually deciding to enroll at San Diego State.{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/recruiting/basketball/national/2007-12-21-basketball.htm |title=Top underclassmen square off at invitational |access-date=January 1, 2008 | work=USA Today | date=December 21, 2007 |first=Jerry |last=Meyer}} Gordon was warmly welcomed by Indiana fans, but received sharp criticism from Illinois fans for publicly maintaining to the press his commitment to playing at Illinois until just a few weeks before he signed with Indiana. Eric Sr. stated in October 2006 that his son had received death threats as a result of his decision,{{cite news |url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=CSTB&p_theme=cstb&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=114EDA77DFE275D8&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM |title=Sports culture out of whack |access-date=January 1, 2008 | work=Chicago Sun-Times | first=Greg | last=Couch | date=October 22, 2006}} but his son later stated that Illinois fans had only said they did not want the younger Gordon to be successful.{{cite web |url=http://www.hoopsusa.com/f_viewtopic.cfm?trnbr=4527 |title=Gordon saga costly for Lincoln Park |access-date=February 9, 2008 |archive-date=September 28, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100928234633/http://hoopsusa.com/f_viewtopic.cfm?trnbr=4527 |url-status=dead }} On February 7, 2008, when Gordon and Indiana played Illinois in Champaign, he was the target of loud booing and taunting throughout the game. Illinois fans were reportedly particularly enraged that the Gordon family, and its entourage, wore "Got Gordon?" T-shirts. At one point during the game, Eric Sr. stood up, turned around facing away from the court, and "flipped off" the Illinois fans, which caused fans to focus their ire on Gordon Sr. rather than just his son. Some witnesses reported that his parents were hit with ice, empty plastic water bottles, and orange-and-blue beads near the game's end.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/columns/story?columnist=forde_pat&id=3236182&sportCat=ncb |access-date=February 8, 2008 |title=Illini seethe hatred toward Eric Gordon, but IU wins anyway|date=February 8, 2008 }} Illinois's athletic director, [[Ron Guenther]], apologized for the incident, calling fan behavior "disappointing and intolerable."{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=3237782 |access-date=February 8, 2008 |title=Illinois apologizes for 'profanity and behavior' aimed at Gordon}} ==College career== Gordon attended [[Indiana University Bloomington]] (IU). There he played shooting guard with the Hoosiers for one year and planned to study sports management. During his year at IU, Gordon attained many honors. He was the Big Ten Freshman of the Year and made the third team All-American. He is IU's all-time leading freshman scorer. He set a record at IU and in the Big Ten with 669 points. He was a candidate for the Wooden Award and Naismith Award, and was named second-team All-American for [[CBSSports.com]]. He wore number 23, as he did in high school. Gordon finished his freshman season averaging 20.9 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per game, making 33.7% of his three-point shots and leading the Big Ten in scoring.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3431/eric-gordon |access-date=April 4, 2008 |title=Eric Gordon Stats, News, Photos}} He was highly effective for Indiana in his first 18 games as the Hoosiers started the season with 17 wins and only one loss, but entered into a noticeable shooting slump at the end of the year,{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/printedition/sports/20080313/c3focusside13.art.htm |title=Gordon confident his shooting slump won't last |access-date=April 4, 2008 | work=USA Today | date=March 12, 2008}} making only 18.6% of his three-point field goal attempts (13 of 70) after Indiana's February 7 win against Illinois and shooting only 3 of 15 from the field and 0-of-6 from the three-point line in the team's loss to [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] in the first round of the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2008 NCAA tournament]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000048 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709065118/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000048 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 9, 2018 |access-date=April 4, 2008 |title=Arkansas vs. Indiana – Recap}} Gordon played the second half of the season with an injured wrist.{{cite web |url=http://blogs.heraldtimesonline.com/iusp/?p=1441 |title=Eric Gordon's wrist |access-date=February 6, 2009 |date=January 29, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080131212030/http://blogs.heraldtimesonline.com/iusp/?p=1441 |archive-date=January 31, 2008 |url-status=dead }} On March 10, 2008, Gordon was named Big Ten Freshman of the Year and to the First Team of the Big Ten Conference by the coaches and media, along with his teammate [[D. J. White]]. He was also a third-team All-American.{{cite web |url=http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20080310/SPORTS/80310071 |title=IU's White: conference player of year |publisher=Indianapolis Star |date=March 10, 2008 |access-date=March 10, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319203838/http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20080310%2FSPORTS%2F80310071 |archive-date=March 19, 2012 }} Gordon announced on April 4, 2008, at 4:00pm at the [[Jewish Community Center]] that he would enter the [[2008 NBA draft]].{{cite web |date=April 4, 2008 |title=Hoosiers' Gordon to enter NBA draft |url=http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20080404/SPORTS0601/804040406 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080407194631/http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20080404%2FSPORTS0601%2F804040406 |archive-date=April 7, 2008 |access-date=April 4, 2008 |publisher=Indianapolis Star}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2008–2011)=== He was drafted with the seventh pick in the 2008 NBA draft by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/gordon_080702.html|title=Clippers Sign Eric Gordon|work=Los Angeles Clippers|publisher=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2008|access-date=February 22, 2023}} Gordon scored 23 points in his first [[NBA Summer League]] game in the Las Vegas summer league on the campus of [[UNLV]]. Gordon played in two summer league games where he averaged 19 points and 6.5 rebounds. Gordon injured his hamstring July 12 against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. It was confirmed on July 13, 2008, by the Clippers that Gordon would miss the rest of summer league due to a [[strained left hamstring]]. However, at the start of the 2008 NBA pre-season, Gordon made his offensive prowess known in only his second exhibition game, scoring 33 points in 31 minutes to help the Clippers defeat the [[Sacramento Kings]] 116–112.PRO BASKETBALL: [http://www.latimes.com/sports/basketball/nba/clippers/la-sp-clippers16-2008oct16,0,5267124.story "Rookie Gordon scores 33 in victory"]. – ''[[Los Angeles Times]]''. – October 16, 2008. On January 23, he set a Clippers franchise record for most points scored by a rookie with 41 points (a record since broken by [[Blake Griffin]]).{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/290123012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211007210939/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/290123012|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 7, 2021|title=Thunder vs. Clippers – Game Recap – January 23, 2009 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com}} With Gordon's exceptional performance, he was named the NBA Western Conference Rookie of the Month for January. He averaged 16.1 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.0 steals in 34.3 minutes per game and was the third leading scorer among all rookies. For his efforts, he was unanimously selected to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] and finished fifth in [[NBA Rookie of the Year|Rookie of the Year]] voting. Gordon participated in the [[2010 NBA All-Star Weekend]]. During the 2010 NBA All-Star Weekend, Gordon and [[DeMar DeRozan]] went head-to-head in the inaugural Sprite All-Star Slam Dunk-In, which took place at halftime of the Rookie Challenge. The fans went on to choose DeRozan as their vote to advance to the main event, the Sprite [[Slam Dunk Contest]]. Gordon was also selected to the sophomore team for the 2010 [[T-Mobile NBA Rookie Challenge and Youth Jam]] event. Gordon finished second on his team with 16.9 points, averaged 2.6 rebounds, 3.0 assists in a team-high 36.0 minutes. He appeared in 62 games, and started in 60 games. He led his team in scoring 16 times, steals 17 times and minutes 16 times. Gordon scored 30-plus points once and had 20-plus points 19 times. He was one of 27 players named to 2010–12 USA Men's National Team Program. After winning the gold medal in the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], Gordon was geared towards a breakout season. Gordon was on a scoring tear earlier in the season but was slowed down in his game against the [[Golden State Warriors]], with a hard foul committed by [[Andris Biedriņš]], which forced Gordon (who was averaging 24.1 points per game before the injury) to be sidelined for 18 games. It was later revealed that Gordon had a sprained wrist with a bone chip fracture. Returning from an 18-game absence, Gordon had a solid performance with a win against the [[Houston Rockets]] with 24 points. Gordon re-aggravated his sprained wrist the second game back against the [[Denver Nuggets]], this time a hard foul committed by [[Timofey Mozgov]], which gave Gordon a six-game absence. Gordon's breakout season was hampered by injuries and he had to wear a wristband for the remainder of the season. Gordon finished the season as the Clippers' second-leading scorer, with 22.3 points per game. He also averaged 2.9 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game. Gordon scored 30-plus points eight times and had a streak of 20 or more points for 12 consecutive games. ===New Orleans Hornets / Pelicans (2011–2016)=== ====2011–2013: First years in New Orleans==== On December 14, 2011, the Clippers traded Gordon, [[Chris Kaman]], [[Al-Farouq Aminu]], and a 2012 first-round pick (previously acquired from the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]) to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in exchange for future teammate [[Chris Paul]] and two future second-round picks.{{cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_clippers_trade_2011_12_14.html|title=HORNETS ACQUIRE GORDON, AMINU, KAMAN AND FIRST ROUND PICK | work=[[NBA.com]]|date=December 14, 2011 | access-date=December 15, 2011}} In his first ever game as a Hornet, playing against the [[Phoenix Suns]], Gordon recorded 20 points, 4 rebounds, and 3 assists. He also hit the game winning shot with 4.2 seconds remaining, and New Orleans defeated the Suns in the season opener 85–84. It was revealed that Gordon had a pre-existing knee injury that he aggravated during the opening game of the season against the Phoenix Suns after bumping knees with [[Grant Hill]]. Initially Gordon was diagnosed with having a bone bruise, but after further examinations by doctors, it was determined that Gordon had cartilage damage in his right knee. On February 14, 2012, Gordon underwent successful arthroscopic surgery on his knee and was out of action for 6 weeks. Gordon returned on April 4, 2012, to face the Denver Nuggets and scored 15 points giving the New Orleans Hornets a 94–92 victory.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/320404003|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230222015104/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/320404003|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 22, 2023|title=Eric Gordon scores 15 in return, leads New Orleans over Denver|work=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|date=April 4, 2012|access-date=February 22, 2023|location=New Orleans}} Gordon finished the season with 9 games played, averaging 20.6 points per game, 2.8 rebounds per game and 3.4 assists per game. He entered the summer of 2012 as a restricted free agent. On July 11, 2012, Gordon signed an offer sheet with the [[Phoenix Suns]] reportedly worth $58 million for four years.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/gordon_120711 | title=Suns Sign Gordon to Offer Sheet, Trade Nash |work=NBA.com | date=July 11, 2012|access-date=July 12, 2012}} On July 14, 2012, the Hornets matched the four-year offer sheet.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_match_offer_for__2012_07_14.html|title=HORNETS MATCH OFFER FOR ERIC GORDON |work=NBA.com | date=July 14, 2012|access-date=July 14, 2012}}[[File:Eric Gordon Hornets.jpg|thumb|Gordon with the Hornets in March 2013]] During the offseason, Gordon admitted that he faced lingering problems with his knee. [[Microfracture surgery]] was reportedly proposed as a solution, but in early November, Gordon received a second opinion from a doctor in Chicago, who prescribed continued rehab or his knee and estimated that Gordon would miss 4–6 weeks.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8584181|title=Report: No surgery needed for Hornets' Gordon|date=November 2, 2012|website=ESPN.com}} On November 7, 2012, Gordon was sent to Los Angeles to get more personalized rehabilitation work to help in his knee recovery and to strengthen his quad muscles. On December 29, 2012, Gordon made his highly anticipated season debut against the Charlotte Bobcats. Gordon, coming off the bench, scored 24 points, 7 assists and 2 steals in less than 25 minutes, giving the New Orleans Hornets a 98–95 win over the Bobcats. Team doctors placed Gordon on strict restrictions from playing in the second game of back-to-back sets and from playing over 30 minutes to avoid overworking his right knee. On January 5, 2013, Gordon returned to the starting lineup. Gordon hit the game-winner with 4.7 seconds left after drawing a foul on [[Dallas Mavericks]] guard [[Darren Collison]], to help the New Orleans Hornets edged the Mavericks 99–96 in overtime. On April 10, 2013, Gordon played his first back-to-back set of the season against the Sacramento Kings after he was cleared by team doctors for his restrictions to be lifted. Gordon finished the season as the Hornets' leading scorer, with 17.0 points per game, 1.8 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game in 42 games played. In April 2013, the Hornets were renamed the New Orleans Pelicans. ====2013–2016: First season in playoffs and injuries==== [[File:20140101 Eric Gordon2.JPG|thumb|Gordon with the Pelicans in January 2014]] On November 29, 2013, Gordon recorded 26 points and 7 assists in a 121–105 win over the Philadelphia 76ers. On January 15, 2014, he recorded 35 points, on 11-for-17 shooting from the field, and 6 assists, in a 100–103 loss to the Houston Rockets. On March 4, 2014, Gordon scored 28 points and was 9-for-13 from the field, including 4-for-5 on threes, and made each of his six attempts from the free throw line. His all-around offense sparked the Pelicans to a 132–125 road win and ended an eight-game losing skid.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gordoer01/gamelog/2014/|title=Eric Gordon 2013–14 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} On March 21, 2014, Gordon left the game in the first quarter against the Hawks. It was later ruled he had knee tendinitis. On April 10, 2014, it was ruled that Gordon will have arthroscopic surgery performed on his left knee, which brought his season to a close.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-injury-update-41014|title=Pelicans Injury Update (4/10/14)|website=New Orleans Pelicans}} Gordon finished the 2013–14 season averaging 15.4 points per game, 2.6 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game in 64 games.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/2013-14-season-review-eric-gordon|title=2013–14 Season in Review: Eric Gordon|website=New Orleans Pelicans}} After averaging 9.5 points per game over the first 12 games of the season, Gordon was ruled out indefinitely with a left shoulder injury on November 24, 2014.
